name: Public-Facing Transactional Service
description: A pattern for citizen-facing digital services that process transactions, collect information, or deliver outcomes. Designed for GOV.UK-style services that must meet the Service Standard, handle sensitive data, and provide reliable, accessible user journeys with audit trails.
whenToUse: Citizen-facing services where users complete transactions such as applications, registrations, or payments
Services that must meet the GOV.UK Service Standard and pass service assessments
Digital services handling OFFICIAL or OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE citizen data
Services requiring audit trails, data retention, and GDPR compliance
High-availability services where downtime directly impacts citizens
whenNotToUse: Internal-only tools used exclusively by civil servants
Services with no transactional element or user data collection
Batch processing systems with no real-time user interaction
Services handling SECRET or TOP SECRET data requiring specialist hosting
Simple informational content that could be served as a static website

typicalComponents.name: Web Application
typicalComponents.purpose: Serve accessible HTML forms and manage user journeys through multi-step transactions
typicalComponents.technology: Node.js with GOV.UK Frontend, or Python with Flask/Django

typicalComponents.name: Application Database
typicalComponents.purpose: Store transaction data, user submissions, and application state

typicalComponents.name: Session Store
typicalComponents.purpose: Manage user sessions across stateless application instances

typicalComponents.name: Message Queue
typicalComponents.purpose: Decouple transaction processing from user-facing responses for reliability
typicalComponents.technology: SQS, Azure Service Bus, or Pub/Sub

typicalComponents.name: Notification Service
typicalComponents.purpose: Send confirmation emails and SMS to citizens after transactions

typicalComponents.name: Payment Gateway
typicalComponents.purpose: Process payments securely with PCI DSS compliance

securityControls: Implement CSRF protection on all form submissions
Encrypt all data at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2+
Implement rate limiting and brute-force protection on authentication endpoints
Apply input validation and output encoding to prevent injection attacks
Implement session timeout and secure cookie attributes
Conduct regular penetration testing and vulnerability scanning
Implement audit logging for all data access and modifications
resilienceConsiderations: Deploy across multiple availability zones for high availability
Implement health checks and automatic instance replacement
Use message queues to prevent data loss during downstream failures
Implement circuit breakers for external service integrations
Design idempotent transaction processing to handle retries safely
Implement graceful degradation when non-critical services are unavailable
costConsiderations: Compute costs scale with user traffic — consider auto-scaling policies
Database costs include storage, IOPS, and backup retention
GOV.UK Notify and Pay are free at point of use for government services
Consider reserved instances for baseline capacity to reduce costs
Factor in penetration testing and security assessment costs
Budget for ongoing accessibility audits and service assessments
operationalConsiderations: Requires 24/7 monitoring and on-call support for citizen-facing availability
Regular patching cycles for application dependencies and OS
Database backup and restore procedures must be tested regularly
Incident response procedures aligned with GDS service management
Performance testing required before major releases or traffic events
Accessibility testing with assistive technologies required for each release

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.purpose: Message queuing for async transaction processing

services.name: AWS WAF + Shield
services.purpose: Web application firewall and DDoS protection

services.name: Azure App Service
services.purpose: Managed web application hosting with deployment slots

services.name: Azure Front Door + WAF
services.purpose: Global load balancing with security policies

services.name: Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL)
services.purpose: Managed relational database with HA configuration

services.name: Memorystore (Redis)
services.purpose: Managed Redis for sessions and caching

questionsToAsk: What is the expected transaction volume and peak usage pattern?
What data classification applies to the information being collected?
Is GOV.UK Notify and Pay integration required or are alternatives acceptable?
What are the availability and recovery time requirements?
Are there integration requirements with existing back-office systems?
What is the team's experience with the GOV.UK Service Standard assessment process?
commonMistakes: Building custom notification or payment systems instead of using GOV.UK platform services
Not designing for accessibility from the start, leading to costly retrofitting
Storing session state in application memory rather than an external session store
Not implementing idempotency for transaction processing, causing duplicate submissions
Underestimating the operational burden of running a 24/7 citizen-facing service
Failing to plan for service assessment checkpoints during delivery
